modules.title: Introduction to Human Rights
modules.html:
Human rights in the Universal Declaration and the fundamental rights in the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria. This section covers introduction to human rights.

Key points

  • The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was adopted by the United Nations on _____. — December 10, 1948.
  • Human rights are said to be 'inalienable' because _____. — They cannot be taken away from an individual.
  • Which article of the UDHR states that 'All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights' — Article 1.
  • One of the following is a limitation to human rights _____. — State of emergency.
  • Which of these is a limitation to human rights — State of Emergency.

Worked examples

Q: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was adopted by the United Nations on _____.
A: December 10, 1948 — The United Nations General Assembly adopted the UDHR on December 10, 1948, at the Palais de Chaillot in Paris.

Q: Human rights are said to be 'inalienable' because _____.
A: They cannot be taken away from an individual — Inalienable rights are rights that cannot be surrendered, transferred, or taken away. They are inherent to all human beings.

examples.q: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was adopted by the United Nations on _____.
Human rights are said to be 'inalienable' because _____.
examples.a: They cannot be taken away from an individual

quiz.q: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was adopted by the United Nations on _____.
quiz.solution: The United Nations General Assembly adopted the UDHR on December 10, 1948, at the Palais de Chaillot in Paris.

quiz.q: Human rights are said to be 'inalienable' because _____.
options: They are only for the rich
They cannot be taken away from an individual
They are given by the government
quiz.solution: Inalienable rights are rights that cannot be surrendered, transferred, or taken away. They are inherent to all human beings.

quiz.q: Which article of the UDHR states that 'All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights'?
quiz.solution: Article 1 is the foundational principle of the UDHR, asserting the freedom and equality of all humans from birth.

quiz.q: One of the following is a limitation to human rights _____.
quiz.solution: During a state of emergency, the government may legally suspend certain human rights to maintain public order.

quiz.q: Which of these is a limitation to human rights?
quiz.solution: During a State of Emergency, the government may legally suspend certain individual rights to maintain public security.
